summary: Art/production review of the five flagship figures in Output/summary/. Closest to publication-ready: Hero_timing.png — clean hierarchy, honest open-marker treatment of the 11 GeV purity caveat, legend doubles as the result; it needs exactly one fix (subtitle strike-through) plus production format. Furthest: Tertiary11.png — four panels of unrebinned single-count log-comb histograms with the largest event class drawn in near-invisible grey; it is Extended Data material, not a cover figure, and needs redesign or demotion. Ranked fixes: (1) CRITICAL, shared root cause: grey subtitles drawn below the frame top edge (radStyle.h:31 sets top margin 0.085, so the frame top is at NDC y=0.915) get struck through by the frame line and ticks — Hero_timing subtitle at y=0.905 (ModuleCompare.C:64) and ALL FOUR HowItWorks step explainers at y=0.90 (HowItWorks.C:52); move to y>=0.918 or widen the top margin. This one coordinate bug degrades two of the five flagships. (2) MAJOR caption accuracy: HowItWorks panel 2 calls the MCP "the ~10 ps reference clock" (HowItWorks.C:71) while the campaign's own diagonal-difference analysis (Output/run_12/FINDINGS.md) measured 107-114 ps reference jitter — quote the measured number or say "MCP reference (device spec ~10 ps; measured jitter ~110 ps)". (3) MAJOR: ModuleCompare right panel y-axis title overprints the 5-digit tick labels ("10000"/"12000" struck through; Y title offset 1.55 in radStyle.h:38 is too small) — use units of 10^3 ADC-eq or offset ~1.9; also the figure has no title/subtitle and no (a)/(b) tags so it cannot stand alone, and the left log axis shows only the 10^2/10^3 decade labels (enable MoreLogLabels). The EJ199 trend omission is handled honestly (points only, legend states "photostatistics-limited (no stable trend)"; the 1218/sqrt(E) TF1 at ModuleCompare.C:71-72 is defined but deliberately never drawn — either delete the dead code or draw it dotted and labeled as the photostatistics expectation, which would be more informative and still honest). (4) MAJOR: PulseShapes traces are clipped at the frame floor (ymin=-0.04, PulseShapes.C:73) so each curve "ends in midair" at a different time (DSB1 ~32 ns, EJ199 ~37 ns, LuAG ~59 ns) and the right quarter of the panel (60-80 ns) is empty — deepen ymin, add a zero line, and crop x to ~45-60 ns; the 0.4 ns rebin has killed the DRS4 comb, leaving only mild acceptable ripple on the LuAG tail. (5) MAJOR: Tertiary11 rebin >=4x, give the dominant "miss" class real visual weight, drop or ratio-ize the interleaved red-dashed reference, and add a one-line takeaway; or move it to Extended Data. (6) PRODUCTION, all figures: PNG-only output at 1496-1996 px (~150 dpi at column width) — Nature requires vector or >=300 dpi; add .pdf SaveAs alongside every .png. (7) MINOR consistency: unit/sign conventions drift across the set ("1-11 GeV" range on Hero, "-7 GeV beam" on PulseShapes, "-11 GeV" on Tertiary11, axis "beam energy [GeV]" vs subtitle "GeV/c") — pick positive energies with a single polarity note.

plots.what_it_shows: The headline result: shower-time resolution vs beam energy for the two viable channels, DSB1 (teal, solid fit, 323 ps/sqrt(E) + 79 ps) and LuAG (red, dashed fit, 389 ps/sqrt(E) + 138 ps), reference included/unsubtracted, with 11 GeV points drawn open to flag the electron-purity caveat. Generated by macros/ModuleCompare.C lines 37-66.
plots.caption_issues: Legend formulas and the subtitle caveat match the documented scan results and FINDINGS.md exactly. Minor: subtitle mixes units — energies quoted as 'GeV' but the purity threshold as '~10 GeV/c' (ModuleCompare.C:64); T10 delivers momentum, pick one convention. Nit: nothing states these are median-of-4-capillary times — fine if the print caption says so, but the figure is otherwise built to stand alone.
plots.design_issues: CRITICAL: the grey subtitle at NDC y=0.905 (ModuleCompare.C:64) sits below the frame top edge at y=0.915 (radStyle.h:31, top margin 0.085) — the frame line and top ticks strike straight through 'CERN PS T10, tagged electrons...', rendering it near-illegible; move to y>=0.918 or enlarge the top margin. That is the only real flaw: hierarchy (30pt title / 26pt legend / 21pt subtitle) is right, open-marker masking of the dashed curve at 11 GeV is cleanly done via the white-underlay trick (lines 50-55), marker size 1.6 vs 2-3 px error bars is balanced (bars smaller than markers at low E, which is honest — errors ARE that small). MINOR: dashed-vs-solid fit-line distinction is unexplained (harmless, aids grayscale). NIT: y-axis title 'shower-time resolution  sigma_t  [ps]' has doubled spaces. PRODUCTION: 1496x922 PNG only (~150 dpi at column width); emit a PDF. Closest to publication-ready of the five.
plots.physics_questions: None of substance. The 1 GeV DSB1 point sits visibly below its own fit curve while the fit hugs 3-9 GeV — a chi2 or a note on which points constrain the fit would preempt a referee question about the stochastic term.

plots.what_it_shows: Two-panel three-channel comparison: left, log-y timing resolution with EJ199 (amber) added as points-only above the DSB1/LuAG fits; right, summed low-gain peak response vs energy showing DSB1 collecting ~2.1x LuAG's light and EJ199 tracking LuAG. Generated by macros/ModuleCompare.C lines 68-96.
plots.caption_issues: The EJ199 omitted-trend handling is honest and correctly worded: points only, legend states 'photostatistics-limited (no stable trend)', and the 11 GeV response omission is declared in the right legend ('11 GeV fit unstable, omitted'). Two gaps: (1) the 1218/sqrt(E) photostatistics fit the campaign log cites exists in the code (fJ, ModuleCompare.C:71-72) but is never drawn — dead code; drawing it dotted, labeled as the photostatistics expectation, would be MORE informative and equally honest. (2) The right panel silently starts at 3 GeV — 1 GeV response points for all three channels are omitted (pL[0]=pD[0]=0, lines 20/24, plotted from index 1 at lines 87-88) with no note. Minor: '~2.1x the light' (line 92) lacks its referent (vs LuAG).
plots.design_issues: MAJOR: right-panel y-axis title 'SigmaLG peak [ADC-eq]' overprints the 5-digit tick labels — the leading digits of '10000' and '12000' are struck through (Y title offset 1.55, radStyle.h:38, too small for 5 digits); relabel in units of 10^3 ADC-eq or push the offset to ~1.9. MAJOR: no figure title, no subtitle, no (a)/(b) panel tags — the only flagship with zero headline text; it cannot stand alone and is inconsistent with its siblings. MAJOR: left log axis carries only the 10^2 and 10^3 decade labels across data spanning 133-1367 ps — the reader cannot read off any value or quantify the DSB1-LuAG gap; enable MoreLogLabels or use custom ticks at 100/200/500/1000. MINOR: left legend (0.36-0.93 NDC, line 80) crowds the EJ199 5 GeV point. PRODUCTION: PNG only, 1996x872.
plots.physics_questions: Right panel shows LuAG response flat/falling from 9 to 11 GeV (5782 -> 5696, open marker) — consistent with the documented purity caveat plus gain ladder, but a stand-alone reader will read it as saturation, which the campaign explicitly retired; consider suppressing the open response points entirely or annotating. Is the +-15% cross-run SiPM gain-ladder systematic represented anywhere in these error bars? The bars look statistical-only, which understates the response uncertainty.

plots.what_it_shows: Mean tagged-electron pulse shapes at -7 GeV for the three channels (runs 27/33/42), peak-aligned and peak-normalized, with the legend carrying the physics: DSB1 tail tau=5 ns/16% after 8 ns, LuAG 12 ns/32%, EJ199 6 ns/25% — the scintillation-decay case for DSB1's timing advantage. Generated by macros/PulseShapes.C.
plots.caption_issues: Run/channel/energy assignments check out against the registry (27=LuAG, 33=DSB1, 42=EJ199, all 7 GeV) and the tail numbers are computed live from the data (lines 46-59), so legend and data cannot drift apart — good practice. Nits: '-7 GeV beam' is a signed momentum written as an energy (line 87); title 'by capillary channel' is ambiguous — elsewhere 'capillary 4-7' means the four capillaries of one set, here it means the three materials; say 'by capillary material'.
plots.design_issues: MAJOR: all three traces are clipped at the frame floor (ymin=-0.04, PulseShapes.C:73) where the mean undershoot dips below it, so each curve 'ends in midair' at a different time (DSB1 ~32 ns, EJ199 ~37 ns, LuAG ~59 ns) — at cover standard this reads as missing data; deepen ymin to ~-0.10, draw a zero reference line, and let the traces complete. MAJOR: the right ~25% of the panel (60-80 ns) is empty ink-free whitespace — crop x to ~45-60 ns, which also enlarges the physics-bearing region. MINOR: subtitle drawn inside the plot frame at y=0.865 (line 87), brushing the left frame edge and top ticks — move above the frame at the Hero's (fixed) position for set consistency. Comb check: the deliberate 0.4 ns rebin (2 samples/bin, line 65) has eliminated the DRS4 sampling comb; only low-amplitude correlated ripple survives on the LuAG tail (20-55 ns) — acceptable, though a 3-bin smooth would polish it. CODE NIT: on line 65 'pL->SetDirectory(nullptr);' is trapped inside the trailing comment and never executes. PRODUCTION: PNG only, 1496x922.
plots.physics_questions: The window starts at -5 ns with all traces already at 0.2-0.4 of peak, so the rising edge — the part timing is actually extracted from (15% threshold crossing) — is mostly cropped out; extending to ~-10 ns would let the figure support the timing story, not just the tail story. Are the sub-zero tails genuine electronics undershoot or baseline-estimation bias from the 40-sample pre-window (line 37)? Worth one caption clause, since normalized negative light bothers referees.

plots.what_it_shows: Lay-reader four-step measurement walkthrough on mean 5 GeV waveforms (run 15): 1 electron ID via the two XCET Cherenkovs, 2 MCP time reference, 3 energy from the summed 2x2 low-gain peaks, 4 timing from the high-gain 15% threshold crossing. Generated by macros/HowItWorks.C.
plots.caption_issues: MAJOR: panel 2's subtitle calls the MCP 'the ~10 ps reference clock' (HowItWorks.C:71), but the campaign's own diagonal-difference analysis measured and validated 107-114 ps of reference jitter (Output/run_12/FINDINGS.md) — the figure understates the measured reference term by 10x and contradicts the paper's ref-subtraction narrative; write 'MCP reference (measured jitter ~110 ps)' or drop the number. Minor: panel 4's subtitle says '15% of its PREDICTED peak' while the dashed line is drawn at 15% of the mean waveform's own peak (line 89) — acceptable as illustration, but the predicted-vs-actual distinction is what makes the method work and is silently lost.
plots.design_issues: CRITICAL for this figure's purpose: all four grey step explanations at NDC y=0.90 (HowItWorks.C:52) collide with the frame top edge at 0.915 — frame line and tick marks strike through every one ('both gas Cherenkov counters fire...', etc.), and these lines ARE the lay narrative; with them unreadable the figure is four unexplained oscilloscope traces. Same one-line fix as Hero_timing. MAJOR: panel 3 shows a visible discontinuity/kink in all four capillary curves at ~127 ns and an end-of-window droop at ~203 ns — unexplained instrumental artifacts in a didactic figure; cropping x to ~120 ns (pulses peak at ~75 ns) removes both and tightens every panel (panels 1, 2, 4 are >50% empty on the right as-is, since all signals finish by ~100 ns). MINOR: the numbered story says 'when did it arrive' but panel 1's Cherenkov pulses sit at ~85-90 ns while panel 2's MCP peaks at ~12 ns — different channel-group window offsets make the arrival-time story visually incoherent for the intended lay reader; align time origins or note the offset. MINOR: panel 4 never marks the actual threshold crossing — 'The precise moment' needs a vertical line or arrow at the crossing point. NIT: legend 'capillary 4/5/6/7' exposes DAQ slot numbers; a 2x2 position labeling would serve the lay reader better. PRODUCTION: PNG only, 1996x1122.
plots.physics_questions: What causes the coherent ~127 ns step in the four low-gain mean waveforms (panel 3)? If it is a DRS4 window/stitching or spike-removal artifact it should be cropped or footnoted before a referee asks; if it is real (e.g. reflections), it belongs in the text, not silently in the flagship explainer.

plots.what_it_shows: The 11 GeV purity forensics: for LuAG and DSB1, tagged Sigma-LG spectra split into miss/partial/contained classes overlaid with the scaled 9 GeV tag shape (top row, with contained counts and E-equivalents 9.7/8.0 GeV), and MCP pulse-height spectra by class vs the ~97%-pion untagged population (bottom row). Generated by macros/Tertiary11.C.
plots.caption_issues: Class counts, E-equivalents, and the '~97% pi' untagged composition all match the documented 11 GeV caveat (contained tags are hard electrons; halo unexplained), and open questions are not papered over. Nits: '9 GeV tags (scaled)' never states the scaling (area-normalized to what?); the title's '-11 GeV' polarity-signed momentum clashes with 'beam energy 1-11 GeV' phrasing elsewhere in the set.
plots.design_issues: MAJOR — information overload, the furthest of the five from publication-ready: four panels x 3-4 unrebinned step histograms at O(1) counts/bin on log-y produce a picket-fence of single-count spikes carrying most of the ink; the largest class (miss, 467 events, LuAG) is drawn in the faintest grey and visually vanishes; the red-dashed 9 GeV reference interleaves destructively with the orange partial comb; bottom panels bottom out at 1e-4 so empty bins render as floating dashes. Fixes: rebin >=4x, translucent fills for the classes, promote 'miss' to a real color, replace the dashed overlay with a shaded reference band or a ratio strip, and add the missing takeaway subtitle ('contained -11 GeV tags carry electron-like MCP amplitudes and ~9 GeV of light') — at present the headline must be reverse-engineered from the legends. Structurally this is Extended Data, not a cover figure: if the point must live in the main text, one panel (DSB1 Sigma-LG with the 9 GeV band) says it all. PRODUCTION: PNG only, 1996x1122.
plots.physics_questions: The bottom-row message (tagged-contained MCP spectrum resembles the genuine-particle spectrum, with a high-amplitude tail) is the crux of the purity argument but is left implicit — is the intended claim that contained tags are beam electrons while miss tags are halo? A quantitative statement (e.g. KS/chi2 vs the untagged shape, or the tail fraction) would carry it better than four spectra. Also: does the E-eq 8.0 GeV for DSB1-contained vs 9.7 for LuAG-contained reflect the same physics, or the +-15% cross-run gain ladder? A referee will subtract these two numbers.
